<action type="say">
Here’s how to cancel that November 1 JetBlue trip yourself and what to expect.

1) In the JetBlue mobile app
1. Open the JetBlue app and sign in (same account you used to book).  
2. Tap “Trips” or “My trips.”  
3. Find your November 1 reservation and tap it.  
4. Tap “Manage trip” or “Change/Cancel.”  
5. Choose “Cancel flight” / “Cancel trip” (wording may vary).  
6. Make sure:
   - All flights in that reservation are selected  
   - All travelers are selected (if more than one person on the booking)  
7. The app will show a summary screen with:
   - How much goes back to the original form of payment  
   - How much becomes a JetBlue Travel Bank credit (if applicable)  
   - Any fees (if any apply to your fare)  
8. Review the amounts, then tap to confirm cancellation.  
9. You’ll get a cancellation email with a new confirmation/cancellation number and any Travel Bank details.

2) On jetblue.com (web)
1. Go to jetblue.com and click “Manage trips” (or “Manage Trips” in the top menu).  
2. Either:
   - Sign in and select the November 1 trip under “My trips”, or  
   - Enter the confirmation code and last name under “Find a flight.”  
3. Open the reservation, then click “Cancel” or “Cancel trip.”  
4. Confirm you’re canceling the entire itinerary and all travelers.  
5. Review the refund/credit breakdown shown on the confirmation page.  
6. Click to confirm cancellation and save/print the confirmation page or email.

3) What usually happens with refund/credits (high level)
Exact details depend on your fare type and how you paid, but in general:

- Nonrefundable fares (most “Blue” type tickets):
  - No traditional cash refund.  
  - Value usually goes into a JetBlue Travel Bank credit (minus any applicable fees if your fare has them).  
  - You can use Travel Bank credit on future JetBlue flights until it expires (expiration date will be shown in your Travel Bank).

- Refundable fares:
  - You’ll see “Refundable” when you booked, and on the manage-trip screen.  
  - Cancel, and the base fare is typically refunded back to your original form of payment; taxes/fees generally follow the same path.

- Blue Basic (JetBlue’s basic economy):
  - These have the strictest rules. There may be a fee or in some cases limited/no refund depending on your route and current policy.  
  - The cancel screen will explicitly show if there’s a fee and exactly what (if anything) you get back.

- If you used TrueBlue points:
  - Points usually go back to your TrueBlue account.  
  - Taxes/fees paid in cash/credit card go back either to the original card or as a Travel Bank credit, as shown on the confirmation screen.

4) How to know exactly what you’ll get for the Nov 1 booking
Before you hit the final “Cancel” button in the app/website, carefully read the summary box. It should clearly say something like:

- “$X.xx will be returned to your original form of payment”  
- “$Y.yy will be issued as a JetBlue Travel Bank credit”  
- Any fees deducted

If you want, you can stop at that summary screen, take a screenshot, and paste or describe what it shows to me—I can interpret it for you and tell you exactly what it means in practice before you actually confirm the cancellation.</action>
